items.proposed_content: Interpretation: in each compact-character sector over a function field, exact support and Fourier-support constraints become compatible enough that the trace of P̂_ΛP_Λ is not merely an overlap statistic: it is exhausted by an explicitly constructed finite-dimensional intersection. The dimension (2N+1)l−fl+(2−2g)l makes conductor degree f and genus g corrections into counts of admissible translates. This representation gains an exact arithmetic-geometric count from joint concentration, but it depends on positive-characteristic compact-support behavior; it does not furnish the same literal construction at Archimedean places.

items.proposed_content: The pullback operator for a smooth map has a density-valued delta kernel on its graph, and restricting that kernel along the flow diagonal is legitimate under wave-front transversality. For a nonvanishing periodic orbit this transversality is exactly invertibility of 1-P on the quotient by the flow direction. The induced normal-bundle symbol supplies |det(1-P)|^(-1), while pushforward along the fixed set to time supplies the primitive-period or isotropy-covolume factor, producing the periodic-orbit term in the flow trace.

Band-limited approximate units reduce the annihilator of Im(E) to compactly supported distributions satisfying L(X_0,1/2+it) psi_hat(t)=0. Distribution derivatives at zeros, subject to zero order and Sobolev integrability, then describe the cokernel modes and their Jordan structure, from which the trace-class zero sum follows.

items.proposed_content: The quotient construction first completes the codimension-two Bruhat-Schwartz subspace in an adelic orbit-sum seminorm, then embeds it equivariantly by E into a weighted regular representation of the idele class group. Passing from the image of E to its cokernel H changes quotient semantics into a spectral defect: the sector generator D_chi has the critical-line zeros of the corresponding L-function as its discrete spectrum.

items.proposed_content: The local factor |1-u|^(-1) is the transverse fixed-point weight for multiplication on a local field. In the adelic quotient, nontrivial global fixed loci close to the place hyperplanes H_v, whose transverse spaces are k_v and whose isotropy groups are the embedded k_v*. Thus the local fixed-point distributions become a sum indexed by places, and the S-local cutoff theorem gives a rigorous finite-place trace formula with the required principal values.

items.proposed_content: After setting delta=0, joint support and Fourier-support define cutoff subspaces whose image under E lies inside the regular-representation window, so the complementary operator S_Lambda-Q'_Lambda,0 is positive. The global trace formula would identify the limit of its positive-type distributions with the Weil distribution; independently, the limit is computed from zeros by harmonic measure on the critical line. These two descriptions coincide exactly under RH, yielding the stated trace-formula/RH equivalence in positive characteristic.
